title: Where Does Physical Self-Improvement Come From?

beats.visual_focus: A robot arm twitching and failing a simple pick-and-place task repeatedly.

beats.text: The villain is the Physical Barrel; your agent's progress is capped by its weakest, most brittle capability stave.
beats.visual_focus: A barrel with uneven wooden staves leaking water at the lowest point.

beats.text: We shatter this with PhysRSI-Eval, a five-axis metric tracking first-attempt success, efficiency, and recovery under strict interaction budgets.
beats.visual_focus: A dashboard showing five distinct radar chart axes expanding in real-time.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was actually solid—I've seen enough robot fail-compilations to know exactly what you're talking about. But then you lost me. 'Physical Barrel' and 'capability stave' sound like you're trying to force a metaphor that doesn't exist in actual robotics engineering. I'm a CS student, I know what an ablation study is, but 'history-ablated' is just word salad. I want to know how the buffer works, not hear about 'staves' in a barrel.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A barrel where the shortest stave limits the total volume of liquid, representing how specific capability bottlenecks constrain robotic improvement.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Proving that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist to drive recursive self-improvement.
